sections.heading: Overshoot from slow voltage loop
sections.text: Half-bridge overshoot: same as push-pull — the voltage loop is too slow. Switch to peak-current-mode if not already. The split-capacitor midpoint drifts under load step, adding a transient disturbance that the voltage loop must handle.

sections.heading: Slow settling
sections.text: Check: (1) current loop bandwidth f_ci ~ fsw/5, (2) slope compensation not excessive, (3) split-capacitor midpoint recovery. The midpoint drift creates an effective input voltage disturbance that slows settling.

sections.heading: Excess ripple from leakage inductance
sections.text: Leakage inductance ring with MOSFET Coss causes high-frequency oscillation on the primary. Add RCD snubbers. On the secondary, verify the output capacitor ESR is low enough for the ripple spec.

sections.heading: Split-capacitor midpoint drift
sections.text: If the split-capacitor midpoint drifts >5% from V_in/2, the transformer gets a DC bias. Causes: asymmetric gate drive, unequal blanking times, or unbalanced current sensing. Verify per-switch current sensing and symmetric layout.

sections.heading: Architecture limit
sections.text: If the half-bridge cannot handle the power level (>1kW) or the voltage stress exceeds switch ratings, upgrade to full-bridge. Full-bridge uses all four quadrant switches and can deliver twice the power at the same switch stress.
